newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to name Erskine Bowles new chief of staff.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to name Erskine Bowles new chief of staff.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton plans to name Erskine Bowles, a former top White House official and currently a North Carolina investment banker, as his new chief of staff, an administration official said on Friday.
The official, who declined to be identified, said Clinton was likely to announce the appointment at his 3 p.m. EST (2000 GMT) news conference on Friday.
Bowles, 51, will replace Chief of Staff Leon Panetta, who has made no secret of his desire to leave the White House and is believed to be considering making a run for California governor in 1998.
Bowles previously served Clinton as deputy chief of staff at the White House and left that position in December 1995 to return to private life and start a venture capital firm.
Having raised money for Clinton in the South during his 1992 campaign, Bowles was brought to Washington after the election to run the federal Small Business Admistration (SBA) in 1993 and 1994.

He acquired a reputation as a Clinton loyalist at the SBA, and gained the president's ear as a member of the National Economic Council, the White House team that coordinates he administration's economic policy.
Clinton is close to Bowles, having used him for delicate assignments even after his departure from the White House and often seeking him out as a golf partner.

In August, the president asked Bowles to undertake the sensitive task of speaking to top campaign strategist Dick Morris after media reports surfaced that Morris had had a year-long relationship with a prostitute.
Several top officials have made known their plans to quit since Clinton won re-election on Tuesday, including Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defence Secretary William Perry.
Officials say Clinton has worked hardest to find a replacement for the chief of staff, the most powerful job in the White House after the president's.
